heading.en: A school day that history changed

hook.en: Imagine walking into class and hearing that, from tomorrow, you may no longer study in your own mother tongue. That is the shock at the heart of The Last Lesson.

objectives.en: Introduce Alphonse Daudet and the story's origin
Explain the Franco-Prussian War and the loss of Alsace and Lorraine
Identify the narrator and the point of view

narration.en: Imagine walking into class and hearing that, from tomorrow, you may no longer study in your own mother tongue. That is the shock at the heart of The Last Lesson.

body.en: Alphonse Daudet was a nineteenth-century French writer of short stories and novels. The Last Lesson is set in 1870, during the Franco-Prussian War, when Prussia (later the core of Germany) defeated France. The French districts of Alsace and Lorraine passed under Prussian control, and an order came from Berlin that only German would be taught in their schools.

points.en: Place: a village school in Alsace
The trigger: an order from Berlin to teach only German

title.en: From war to the last lesson

narration.en: Let us place the story on a timeline so the history makes sense.

say.en: In 1870 France and Prussia went to war, and Prussia won.
After the defeat, the French districts of Alsace and Lorraine came under Prussian rule.

text.en: Alsace and Lorraine taken by Prussia

say.en: An order came from Berlin that schools there must teach only German.

text.en: Order from Berlin: teach only German

say.en: So M. Hamel had to give his very last French lesson in the village school.
From the next day a new master would teach in German.

explanation.en: Seen through a child's eyes, a political defeat becomes a personal loss.

body.en: The story is told in the first person by Franz, a young schoolboy. Because we see events through a child's eyes, the political tragedy becomes personal: it is about a lost lesson, an unlearnt rule of grammar and a teacher saying goodbye.

points.en: A child's view makes a big historical event feel personal

problem.en: What was the order from Berlin, and how did it affect the school in the story?

steps.en: State the order: only German was to be taught in the schools of Alsace and Lorraine.
Link it to the war: the districts had been taken over by Prussia in 1870.
Show the effect: M. Hamel had to give his last French lesson that day.

answer.en: After Prussia took Alsace and Lorraine in 1870, an order from Berlin said only German would be taught in their schools. So M. Hamel had to give his last French lesson, and a new master would come the next day.
